description:
I am participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. My chosen challenge is "Abandoned but no Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars". I'm interested in space exploration, scientific research, storytelling, and visual communication. I aim to create an informative and engaging project about NASA's abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars 

Also I love astrophysics and how interesting it's to talk about it in simplified language
summary: Keepers of Stardust is a 8-page illustrated educational storybook created for schoolchildren and young space enthusiasts to address the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Many people mistakenly view inactive spacecraft resting on the Moon, Mars, and asteroids as useless "space junk." My project changes this perspective by turning verified NASA mission archives into an inspiring, accessible story about five legendary pioneers: Mars Pathfinder’s Sojourner, the Opportunity rover, the Apollo 11 Lunar Module "Eagle," the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, and the NEAR Shoemaker asteroid probe. Combining emotional storytelling with real launch dates, landing coordinates, mission records, and authentic NASA photography, the book shows how these machines sacrificed themselves to advance planetary science and pave the way for humanity’s future in space
details:
Keepers of Stardust is an interactive 8-page digital science book designed for students and young readers. Each page highlights a historic NASA spacecraft that completed its mission and remains on another celestial body: Sojourner (Ares Vallis,Mars),Opportunity (Meridiani Planum, Mars),Apollo 11 "Eagle" & EASEP (Sea of Tranquility,Moon),Ingenuity (Jezero Crater,Mars),and NEAR Shoemaker (Asteroid 433 Eros). Every chapter pairs engaging,youth-friendly storytelling with a structured "Mission Card" containing exact launch/landing dates,geographic coordinates,and key scientific discoveries

Technical reports and raw planetary data can be intimidating for beginners. By translating official NASA mission histories into a visual storybook,this project inspires young learners to appreciate space exploration,understand the real scientific breakthroughs behind these missions (such as evidence of ancient water on Mars,lunar laser ranging,and extraterrestrial flight),and view historic landing sites as sacred monuments of human curiosity rather than space trash

The book cover was designed using Picsart (combining space stickers,typography, and AI-assisted graphic elements),while the 8-page book layout and 6-slide presentation were created in Canva. All mission facts,timelines, coordinates,and spacecraft photographs were sourced directly from official NASA archives
